headline: Sox Explode For Ten Runs As Sonny Gray Shines At Fenway
morning_brew: Finally, some life at Fenway Park! After weeks of making us want to throw our remotes into the Charles River, the Red Sox came out and absolutely destroyed the Texas Rangers in a ten to one blowout on Friday night. Sonny Gray was absolutely magnificent on the mound, giving up just one run over six strong innings while racking up seven strikeouts. This is the kind of pitching performance we have been begging for all summer, and it completely shut down any hope the Rangers had. It felt like a party in the stands for once, and the energy was exactly what this team needed to snap out of their funk.

The bats finally woke up and started making some serious noise. We hammered out twelve hits, including three-hit nights from Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Willson Contreras. All three of those guys launched home runs, turning the game into an absolute laugher by the middle innings. This lineup was so hot that even Uncle Carmine stayed awake through the eighth inning to watch the fireworks, which is a miracle since the guy usually falls asleep before they even sing the national anthem. If we can keep this level of production going, maybe this season isn't completely lost after all.

Down in Foxborough, the positive vibes are continuing to build as Drake Maye keeps turning heads at minicamp. Word is that superstar receiver A.J. Brown is wicked impressed with the young quarterback's leadership and chemistry. Seeing our franchise quarterback build that connection in June is exactly what we need to keep us sane until training camp opens.

news_digest.headline: A.J. Brown impressed by Drake Maye's leadership at Pats' minicamp
news_digest.dans_take: Love hearing this from a veteran leader, Maye is taking charge of this team early.

news_digest.headline: Rafaela powers Red Sox to 10-1 rout of Rangers as Gray shines on mound
news_digest.dans_take: Now that is how you start a weekend series at Fenway Park.
